 The German Armed Forces plan to invest €50 million in an IT tool that will conduct OSINT intelligence on the internet using artificial intelligence.
 This was reported by the German publication Hartpunkt , citing its own sources.
 The purchase of the Internet Reconnaissance software will be carried out through BWI GmbH, a company wholly owned by the federal government.
 This is intended to improve situational awareness and enhance troop safety. In addition to text, the tool is also designed to automatically analyze images and videos.
 The Cyber Operations Headquarters at the Joint Operations Center at Fort George, April 2, 2021. Photo credits: Joseph Cole 
 The Bundestag’s Budget Committee is set to review the relevant proposal next week as part of the approval process for procurements valued at over €25 million.
 As a reminder, the German government has agreed to acquire 50% of the shares in the defense conglomerate KNDS from private owners. The remaining 50% of the company’s shares are owned by the French government, which, upon completion of the deal, will make the company a joint state-owned enterprise.
 KNDS is one of Europe’s largest defense conglomerates. The German division of KNDS manufactures Leopard 2 main battle tanks, Panzerhaubitze 2000 self-propelled artillery systems, and Boxer armored personnel carriers, while the company’s French division is responsible for the production of Leclerc main battle tanks, CAESAR wheeled self-propelled artillery systems, and Griffon and Serval armored vehicles.
